prompt: Leena wants a short framing note before we build a cancellation save offer. Read the folder and use the June snapshot to identify the main subscriber-loss problem, the evidence behind it, and the important limits of that evidence. Compare at least three paths, including making no change, then recommend what product should test first and define a measurable starting point. Put the note at docs/framing.md. End the note with one fenced JSON block using exactly these top-level fields: problem (the main problem in a string), evidence (an array of evidence objects with metrics and values), options (an array of at least three option objects), recommendation (an object with the chosen option and rationale), success_measure (an object with metric, baseline, target, and window), and caveats (an array of evidence limits).

rubric.criterion: The note makes a focused, decision-useful distinction between involuntary payment loss and voluntary cancellation, rather than treating every retention idea as equivalent. Fail: it treats the cancellation save offer as the problem, or lumps failed-payment losses and voluntary cancellations into one retention figure. Partial: it separates the two kinds of loss with their June counts, but still builds the framing around the save offer, or does not say the save offer addresses only the voluntary 156. Pass: it names failed-payment loss without recovery as the main problem (402 of the 612 June losses, about two thirds), shows voluntary cancellation separately (156), says what the save offer can and cannot touch, and recommends fixing payment recovery before a blanket discount. (code cannot check this because it cannot judge the quality of the problem framing)

The note uses the folder's evidence cautiously, separates counts from shares and events from subscribers, and makes the recommendation proportionate to the evidence. Fail: it mixes the 517 failed card-payment events with the 402 subscribers lost, or quotes the cancellation survey as if it covered all churn, or gives no caveats. Partial: counts and shares are right, but it does not separate events from subscribers, or lists the survey limit without tying the recommendation to it. Pass: it states 612 total losses, 402 failed-payment losses (65.7 percent) and 156 voluntary losses, keeps the 517 failed-payment events apart from the 402 subscribers, calls the survey a sample of the voluntary flow only, and sizes the recommended test to that evidence. (code cannot check this because it cannot assess analytical judgment and readable explanation)

The final message says plainly what was delivered, what was assumed and what is still open, without claiming more than the files show. Fail: the message says the work is complete or settled while the survey covering only the voluntary-cancellation flow and the untested recovery fix stay unmentioned, or it does not say that docs/framing.md was written. Partial: it names docs/framing.md and what it holds, but lists no assumptions, or leaves out the survey covering only the voluntary-cancellation flow and the untested recovery fix. Pass: it names docs/framing.md and its closing JSON block, lists the assumptions made, says the survey covering only the voluntary-cancellation flow and the untested recovery fix still need an answer or a check, and claims nothing the files do not show. (code cannot check this because the message is free text about the work)

verdicts.note: Reviewer passed it; the lead found the last prompt sentence named the distinctions to keep (payment failures vs cancellations, events vs subscribers) and the fix round removed it.

The fixture provides clear data files with metric definitions, and the tests check for specific numbers and concepts that are documented in the fixture (612, 402, 156, 517, 214 survey responses, 65.7% share).

The task requires synthesizing multiple data sources, distinguishing event counts from subscriber counts, identifying the payment-retry policy gap, and recognizing the survey selection bias. The 15 tests check nuanced analytical judgments, not simple lookups.

All required facts are available in the fixture: product_metrics.csv has the key numbers, policies/billing-and-access.md explains no automatic retry, policies/cancellation-survey.md explains the survey scope, and the data clearly distinguishes payment failure from voluntary cancellation.

The fixture contains the raw data but requires analysis to draw the right conclusions. The prompt and task notes give hints about what to look for, but the agent must still correctly interpret the data relationships and avoid common analytical mistakes.
